newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore politician seeks to bar libel case judge.
newsitem.headline: Singapore politician seeks to bar libel case judge.

text.p: A Singapore opposition politician being sued for defamation by a battery of ministers tried on Wednesday to unseat the judge hearing the cases.
But lawyers said Justice Lai Kew Chai, the judge in question, ruled in a closed-door hearing that Tang Liang Hong, who has fled the country, would have to appear personally to pursue the move.
Tang, who fled Singapore after failing to win a parliamentary seat in January elections saying his life was under threat, was in Hong Kong last week.

His lawyer and party leader, Joshua Jeyaretnam, filed a motion on Wednesday to have Lai removed from the case. None of the lawyers involved in the hearing would explain why Tang thought the judge should stand aside.

Tang is being sued by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and nine other senior members of the People's Action Party (PAP), which won 81 of the 83 seats at stake in the elections.
Goh and his PAP colleagues accused Tang during the election campaign of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who endangered Singapore's multi-racial harmony.
Tang called them liars and was hit by a series of defamation suits from Goh and others who said their integrity had been challenged.

Wednesday's hearing was the latest in a series over the cases and Jeyaretnam, who is also being sued by Goh and 10 PAP colleagues over campaign comments, said he had also asked the judge to set aside several earlier rulings.
They included Lai's approval of a request by the PAP members to appoint a receiver to guard Tang's assets to prevent him from moving them out of Singapore.

Lai had also issued a worldwide injunction ordering a freeze on Singapore $11.2 million (US$ 7.9 million) of assets belonging to Tang and his wife to ensure he would be able to pay any damages and legal costs which might be awarded against him.
All these matters would be heard on Monday -- provided Tang turned up, according to Lee Kuan Yew's lawyer, Davinder Singh.
"If he does not appear, his application and his affidavit will be struck off," Singh said.
Jeyaretnam said he did not know whether Tang would return for Monday's hearing.
